title: ADR-004: Google Cloud Pub/Sub for service-to-service events
storage:
Status: Accepted · Date: 2025-11-03 · Deciders: Platform, Scheduling

Context

Scheduling, EVV (electronic visit verification), payroll export and notifications all need to react to visit lifecycle changes (scheduled, clocked in, completed, cancelled). Today they poll the visits table every 30 s. We run entirely on GCP and have two people on the platform team.

Decision

Asynchronous messaging between our services uses Google Cloud Pub/Sub. Each event type gets its own topic with a dead-letter topic; consumers use pull subscriptions.

Alternatives considered

  • Apache Kafka (self-hosted on GKE, Confluent Cloud, or Amazon MSK): rejected. We do not need log compaction or long replay, and running or paying for a Kafka cluster is out of proportion for ~40 msg/s. MSK would also put us cross-cloud.
  • RabbitMQ: rejected. Another stateful system for two people to operate, and no managed offering in our GCP region that the security team has reviewed.

Consequences

Ordering is per ordering key only; consumers must be idempotent. Event schemas live in proto/events.

Revisit when

Sustained volume above 5k msg/s, or a hard requirement for replay longer than 7 days.

title: ADR-006: HERE for geocoding and drive-time routing
storage:
Status: Accepted (2026-01-20). Owner: Scheduling team.

Context

The auto-scheduler assigns caregivers to home visits and needs accurate drive times between patient homes. A lot of our patients live in rural counties where address quality is poor. Geocoding and matrix calls are about 1.2M/month and growing.

Decision

Backend services use the HERE Platform (Geocoding & Search, Matrix Routing) for all geocoding, routing and drive-time estimates. It is wrapped by geo-svc; other services call geo-svc, not HERE directly.

Alternatives considered

  • Google Maps Platform (Geocoding API, Distance Matrix / Routes API): rejected on cost at our volume and because its terms restrict storing results, which the scheduler depends on.
  • Mapbox: rejected; matrix size limits were too small for our daily batch and rural geocoding scored worst in our bake-off.
  • Self-hosted OSRM + Nominatim: rejected, nobody to maintain map data updates.

Exceptions

The patient and caregiver mobile apps may use the platform-native map view (Apple MapKit on iOS, Maps SDK for Android) to display a location or route that geo-svc already computed. The apps must not call any geocoding or routing API themselves.

title: ADR-009: Twilio for patient SMS reminders
storage:
Status: Superseded by ADR-018 (2026-06-30) · Originally accepted: 2025-09-08

Context

Agencies asked for automatic "your nurse is coming tomorrow" texts to reduce missed visits. We need two-way SMS so patients can reply C to confirm.

Decision

The reminders-worker sends patient SMS reminders with Twilio Programmable Messaging using a pool of local numbers per agency.

Alternatives considered

  • Vonage: comparable, slightly cheaper, but nobody had used it.
  • AWS SNS SMS: no two-way support in the way we needed.

Consequences

Twilio credentials live in reminders-worker secrets. Opt-out (STOP) handling relies on Twilio Advanced Opt-Out.

Note 2026-06-30: superseded. See ADR-018 — all patient messaging now goes through notify-svc.

title: ADR-018: All patient messaging goes through notify-svc
storage:
Status: Accepted · 2026-06-30 · Supersedes ADR-009

Context

By mid-2026 four services were sending patient texts on their own (reminders-worker, visits-api, billing-svc, intake). Opt-outs were tracked in three places; a patient who replied STOP to one number still got texts from another. Two state Medicaid audits asked us to prove consent per message, which we could not do.

Decision

All patient- and family-facing SMS, voice calls and email are sent through notify-svc (publish a notification.requested message or call its API). notify-svc owns consent, opt-out, quiet hours and the provider integration (currently Vonage for SMS/voice, Postmark for email). No other service may integrate an SMS, voice or email provider SDK or API directly — this includes Twilio, Vonage, AWS SNS/SES and SendGrid.

Alternatives considered

  • Keep per-service senders with a shared opt-out table: rejected, does not give per-message consent proof.
  • Stay on Twilio inside notify-svc: rejected on price after the 2026 10DLC fee change; we moved to Vonage.

Scope

Internal staff alerting (PagerDuty, Slack alerts to our own on-call) is not patient messaging and is out of scope.

title: Handbook: PHI in logs, metrics and analytics
storage:
This page is part of the Engineering Handbook. Questions go to #security-eng. Last reviewed 2026-02-11.

Why this exists

Our observability and product analytics vendors (Datadog, Sentry, Amplitude) are not covered by the same BAA scope as our databases, and logs are retained for 15 months. One PHI leak into logs means a breach assessment.

The rule

Protected health information must never be written to application logs, metric names or labels, traces, error reports, or product analytics events. PHI here means anything that identifies a patient or their care: name, address, phone, date of birth, MRN, insurance member ID, diagnosis or ICD codes, medications, visit notes. Use the internal patient_id (opaque UUID) when you need to correlate.

How to comply

  • Use the redact() helper for any structured log field that originates from a request body.
  • Sentry SDKs must keep the shared beforeSend scrubber enabled.
  • New analytics event properties are reviewed in the #analytics-schema channel.

Exception

The clinical audit trail (the clinical-audit topic and the audit database behind it) is designed to hold PHI and is exempt. Do not route audit data to Datadog.

title: ADR-012: Audit events for every clinical write
storage:
Status: Accepted · Date: 2026-04-02 · Driver: Compliance (state EVV + HIPAA audit controls)

Context

Agencies must be able to show who changed a visit, care plan or medication list, when, and what the previous value was. Our current answer is "check the DB row's updated_at", which failed an agency's state survey in March.

Decision

Every API endpoint, consumer or job that creates, updates or deletes visit records, care plans or medication lists must emit an AuditEvent (actor, action, entity, before/after) to the clinical-audit topic via the transactional outbox. VisitService, CarePlanService and MedicationService do this automatically; any code that writes those tables without going through them must call AuditPublisher itself.

Alternatives considered

  • Postgres triggers writing to an audit table: rejected, triggers do not know the acting user, and bulk SQL would silently produce events without actor.
  • pgAudit: rejected, statement-level logs are not usable by agencies.

Consequences

Reads do not need audit events. Writes that bypass the services without an audit event fail review.

title: 2026-08-14 Backend guild — notes
storage:
Present: Tomás, Hana, Ade, Luis, Marguerite. Notes: Hana.

1. Incident review INC-212

Release 3.9 renamed visits.clock_in to clock_in_at in the same deploy as the code change. Old pods were still serving for ~6 min during the rolling update and every clock-in failed with "column does not exist". EVV submissions for two agencies were late.

2. Migration practice

Luis proposed blue/green to avoid mixed versions; too expensive for now. Marguerite: we just need to stop shipping breaking migrations.

  • Decision: database schema changes must stay compatible with the version currently running in prod. Use expand/contract: add the new column/table first, move readers and writers over, and only drop, rename or change the type of an in-use column in a later release once nothing deployed uses it. A single migration that renames, drops or retypes a column still read by deployed code is not allowed.

3. Misc

Ade will add a CI check that flags DROP COLUMN/RENAME COLUMN in Alembic files for reviewer attention. Luis to write the expand/contract how-to in the handbook.

title: Mobile guild sync 2026-09-02
storage:
Who: Gwen, Kofi, Sun-hee, Ravi

Topics

  • React Native 0.76 upgrade status — Kofi: iOS done, Android blocked on a Reanimated bug.
  • Pen-test findings on the caregiver app
  • Offline mode for rural visits

Notes

The external pen test (report SEC-41) pulled the refresh token from the caregiver app's AsyncStorage on a rooted Android device in under a minute. Offline mode makes this worse because we want longer-lived sessions. Ravi suggested encrypting AsyncStorage values with a hardcoded key; rejected by the group since the key ships in the bundle.

Outcome

  • Decision: access and refresh tokens in our mobile apps are stored only in the OS secure store (iOS Keychain / Android Keystore, via react-native-keychain). They are never written to AsyncStorage, unencrypted MMKV, SharedPreferences, or plain files.

Follow-ups

  • Sun-hee: migration on first launch after update (read old value, move to Keychain, delete)
  • Gwen: reply to SEC-41

title: Architecture review 2026-10-07: background jobs
storage:
Reviewers: Platform (Tomás, Wen), Scheduling (Priya), Billing (Luis)

Problem

We have background work in at least four shapes: a Celery worker in billing, a BullMQ queue in notify-svc, crontab entries on the bastion host, and a couple of Kubernetes CronJobs. Retries, visibility and on-call are different for each. The 09-28 payroll export ran twice because the bastion cron and a CronJob both had it.

Options discussed

(a) standardise on Celery; (b) Kubernetes CronJobs + a small queue lib; (c) Temporal Cloud. Luis liked Celery because billing already has it, but Redis-backed brokers lost jobs on the last two Redis failovers. CronJobs have no retry history or UI.

Outcome

  • Decision: new background, scheduled and recurring work is implemented as Temporal workflows/activities (Temporal Cloud namespace per env). We will not add new Celery tasks, BullMQ/RQ queues, host crontab entries or Kubernetes CronJobs for recurring work; existing ones are migrated by end of Q1 2027. One-off backfills and data fixes may still run as a plain Kubernetes Job, provided there is a runbook entry.

Next steps

  • Wen: Temporal worker template in platform-libs
  • Luis: list of billing Celery tasks with owners

title: ADR-021: Replace Elasticsearch patient search with Postgres full-text
storage:
Status: Proposed · Date: 2026-11-10 · Author: Hana · review at the 12-02 architecture review

Context

Patient and caregiver search runs on a 3-node Elasticsearch cluster that exists only for this feature. Index lag after edits is ~40 s, and agencies regularly report "I just added the patient and can't find them". The cluster costs more than the primary database.

Proposal

Move patient and caregiver lookup to Postgres full-text search (tsvector + pg_trgm for fuzzy name matching) on the primary database and decommission the Elasticsearch cluster.

Alternatives considered

  • Stay on Elasticsearch and fix lag with refresh tuning: possible, does not address cost.
  • Algolia / Typesense Cloud: rejected, would send patient names to another vendor.

Open questions

Query latency at 2M patients is unmeasured; needs a prototype. Until this ADR is accepted, Elasticsearch remains the search backend.

title: Handbook: EHR and partner integration standards
storage:
Owner: Integrations team · applies to all new partner/EHR work from 2026-05-15

Background

We currently maintain eleven bespoke integrations: CSV over SFTP, two HL7 v2 feeds over MLLP, and a few custom JSON webhooks. Each one breaks differently and only one person understands the HL7 ones.

Standard

New integrations with EHRs and referral partners use FHIR R4 over HTTPS (SMART Backend Services auth), through the fhir-gateway. We do not build new HL7 v2 interfaces, flat-file (CSV/fixed-width) exports or SFTP feeds for partners.

Why not the others

HL7 v2 needs an interface engine (we evaluated Mirth Connect / NextGen Connect and Rhapsody) and specialist knowledge we do not have. Flat files have no schema, no acknowledgement and no auth beyond SSH keys.

Exception

The existing payer billing feed (X12 837 files dropped on the clearinghouse SFTP) stays until the clearinghouse API migration, planned for Q2 2027. Bug fixes and maintenance on that feed are fine; do not add new SFTP feeds alongside it.
